newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice dept contention "speculative" - RG&E.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice dept contention "speculative" - RG&E.

text.p: Rochester Gas and Electric Corp said on Tuesday the U.S. Justice Department's contention that the University of Rochester has somehow been constrained from going into the energy generation and supply business is purely speculative.

Responding to a Justice suit charging a contract to sell low cost power to the university was "anti-competitive" the utility said the school's leadership has never indicated it wants to become a power supplier. The university could not do this without permission of the New York Public Service Commission, RG&E noted.

The utility said it will aggressively defend the contract as being in the best interests of the university by reducing the its electric rates, as well as to RG&E and its other residential, commercial and industrial customers.

The multi-year reduced-rate contract with the university was signed in 1994. It was negotiated in good faith under a policy established, encouraged and supervised by the state commission, RG&E said in a statement.
That policy recognizes the wisdom of keeping large electric customers on RG&E's system so that costs for all other customers remain stable, the company pointed out.
The commission expressly recognized that if the university and other large electric customers built their own generation and went off the RG&E system, the rates to other customers would go up.

The company said it denies that by negotiating and signing the contact, it has engaged in any anti-competitive activity. It should be pointed out that neither the university nor the commission has objected to any part of the agreement and neither has been sued by the government.
"We can only surmise that this lawsuit is the federal government's way of saying it wants to be involved in the electric deregulation process," said RG&E President Thomas Richards.
"We welcome their participation. We believe they should participate through the process established by the PSC, as customers and all other parties have."
The company also pointed out the suit does not challenge any of the other reduced-rate contracts entered into between RG&E and other large customers.
"We will resist any action that attempts to thwart our efforts to legally and correctly bring about lower costs to our customers," Richards said.
